questions.text: Which of these is a solid?
questions.explanation: A wooden block is a solid. It keeps its own shape. Water, milk, and juice are liquids that take the shape of their container.

questions.text: Which word best describes a rock?
questions.explanation: A rock is hard. Hardness is a property we can observe by touching the rock.

questions.text: You want to make a warm winter hat. Which material would work best?
questions.explanation: Wool is soft and holds in heat, so it is a good material for a warm hat. Paper, glass, and metal do not keep you warm.

questions.text: Which change can be undone, so you can get back what you started with?
questions.explanation: Melting an ice cube can be undone. If you freeze the water again, it turns back into ice. Baking, burning, and frying cannot be undone.

questions.text: A big set of small building blocks can be put together to make what?
questions.explanation: A set of small pieces can be taken apart and built into many different objects. The same pieces can make many things.

questions.text: What do plants need to grow?
questions.explanation: Plants need water and sunlight to grow. Without them, a plant cannot make its food and stay healthy.

questions.text: How do many seeds travel to new places to grow?
questions.explanation: Many seeds are carried to new places by the wind or by animals. This helps new plants grow away from the parent plant.

questions.text: Which place would have the MOST different kinds of plants and animals living in it?
questions.explanation: A rainforest is home to many different kinds of plants and animals. A parking lot, road, or sidewalk has very few living things.

questions.text: Which change to the Earth happens QUICKLY?
options: A canyon forming over many years
questions.explanation: A volcano erupting happens quickly. Canyons forming, mountains wearing down, and rocks breaking apart all happen slowly over a long time.

questions.text: Water on Earth can be found as which of these?
options: A solid, a liquid, or a gas
questions.explanation: Water can be a solid (ice), a liquid (water you drink), or a gas (water vapor in the air).

questions.text: Which of these can help stop wind and water from wearing away the land?
questions.explanation: Planting grass and trees helps hold the soil in place, so wind and water cannot wear the land away as easily. Roots grip the ground.

questions.text: On most maps, the color blue is used to show what?
questions.explanation: On a map, blue usually shows water, such as oceans, lakes, and rivers.

questions.text: An engineer wants to solve a problem. What should they do FIRST?
questions.explanation: The first step is to understand the problem. You cannot design a good solution until you know exactly what needs to be fixed.

questions.text: You build two paper bridges and see how many pennies each one holds. Why test both bridges?
options: To compare which design holds more weight
To make the test take longer
To use up all the paper
questions.explanation: Testing both bridges lets you compare them and find out which design works better. Comparing results helps engineers choose the best design.

questions.text: You want to build a small boat that floats. Which material would be best?
questions.explanation: Wood floats on water, so it is the best choice for a boat. A rock, a nail, and sand all sink.

questions.text: A healthy plant is put in a dark closet. It gets water but no light. What will most likely happen?
options: It will grow tall and green
It will turn yellow and weak
questions.explanation: Without light, the plant cannot make its food. It will most likely turn yellow and weak, even if it still gets water.

questions.text: Which change to the land takes a very LONG time?
options: A river slowly carving a canyon
A landslide sliding down a hill
A crack opening in an earthquake
A branch snapping in a storm
questions.explanation: A river carving a canyon takes a very long time, sometimes thousands of years. A landslide, an earthquake crack, and a snapping branch all happen quickly.

questions.text: Before building, an engineer draws a picture or makes a model of their idea. Why?
options: To plan how it will work before building
Because drawing is a rule they must follow
To make the idea look messy
questions.explanation: Drawing a picture or making a model helps an engineer plan how the design will work and share the idea with others before building it.
